decision: Treat Order, ListMode, RBGroups, and Locked as interactive consumer behavior only to the extent the processor actually exposes a layer panel; do not convert optional configuration syntax into a duty to offer alternate configurations.
effective_source: Table 99 expressly describes Order/ListMode/Locked in an interactive PDF processor UI, while Configs is optional and no text requires a UI selector. Table 99's default Order is empty, and groups not listed are not presented.
current_evidence: ADR 0143 and ADR 0246 commit to an interactive Layers tab and tree; Query::Layers -> host panels is current. viewer-core headless tests validate file-to-UI-data and toggle behavior; viewer-ui tests validate common panel interaction.
residual: Nested tree projection remains an assertion gap. VisiblePages now has a separate multi-page defect candidate: current layouts show several pages, but the layer query selects only the current page's group references.

decision: Revise the older optional-content findings: the `/Locked` consumer claim is now evidenced by the current public headless test; keep the prior ListMode corpus test as a positive control, not proof of filtering.
effective_source: Table 99's Locked prohibits UI state changes; VisiblePages displays only groups referenced by one or more visible pages.
current_evidence: `headless.rs::a_locked_group_reaches_a_host_and_its_switch_is_refused` observes flags from a PDF's `/Locked`, then sends commands and asserts independent unlocked movement. `a_visible_pages_list_mode_keeps_the_groups_the_page_reaches` page reaches all groups, so it checks no false exclusion but not filtering behavior. `Open.visible` and current OneColumn arrangements prove the viewer supports multiple simultaneously visible pages; `answers.rs::layers` still filters from `shown_page()` alone.
residual: No broad finding of broken Locked behavior. The two-page VisiblePages candidate is not execution-confirmed until the parent runs `drafts/order_listmode_viewer_query.rs`.

decision: Add a small language matching control that uses one valid Usage application over several OCGs; existing one-group cases cannot verify list-wide exact-match precedence/ties.
effective_source: Table 100 says all exact matches are ON, otherwise all partial matches with Preferred ON are ON, all others OFF.
current_evidence: Implementation computes a list-wide exact set and then the partial preferred set. Existing public rendering test has only one group in each application.
residual: The test draft checks only the stated match algorithm and rendering outcome; it does not impose a policy on malformed tags or change the content language.
